scaleBasis: Bottom horizontal dimension marked 3430 mm, with raster chain ticks approximately (655,1117) and (817,1117): 343 cm / 162 px = 2.1172839506 cm/px. All geometry uses that one uniform scale and translation world=(sourcePixel-(269,81))*scale. Raster is 1536 x 1152; no page-ratio calibration is used.
assumptions: Original source raster is 1536 x 1152 pixels; all walls, quadratic control points, furniture and opening widths use one source-pixel-to-cm transform, with x right and y down.

The printed dimension endpoints are read manually to approximately 1–2 pixels. Other printed chains are not perfectly consistent at this resolution; the scale is a provisional measured raster calibration, not a survey.

Windows omit height, sill and type: semantic-white-model supplies fixed floor-to-ceiling glass. The source does not establish glazing heights. Doors use ordinary editable presentation, even where the source shows double leaves or sliders; their traced width is retained.

Wall height defaults to 280 cm, ordinary wall thicknesses to exterior 20 cm and interior 12 cm. Thin glazed frontage hosts are explicitly 9 cm; these heights and thicknesses are presentation assumptions.
The long living-room frontage and rounded lower perimeter use quadratic curves. Their controls are fitted from visible line-centre evidence, not sampled points asserted to be on the curve.

Balcony B and balcony C dashed outer outlines are treated as railings or limits and omitted from walls. Their open outer boundaries mean automatic floor topology may omit those balcony floor areas. Visible short solid boundary pieces are retained.
The large white notch west of the entry and north of bedroom D is exterior/unknown void; no rooms or partitions are invented there.

The four solid partial foyer arcs are retained as low-confidence unknown partitions. Their function and height are unclear; dashed continuation of the east arc is omitted, and open gaps around these screens remain open.

Bath A has a small swing symbol and a gap in its west partition near the northwest corner; a 30 px ordinary door is hosted there. The thin double line on the bath north edge is retained as a window. Exact frame limits remain approximate.
Bath C entry and the study doorway share a narrow recess. The dashed/fragmented horizontal line inside the bath at about y=725 is treated as a wet-area screen and omitted from architectural walls.

Closet B west access has no clear door swing; it is an editable opening. Furniture is represented only by visible rectangular semantic footprints; heights, styles and plant masses are estimates. No unseen wardrobes, sinks or kitchen runs are invented.
Beds and sofas are individual occupancy blocks; small source decorations, rugs, text, dimension lines, door swing arcs and watermarks are not converted into architectural geometry.
